groups.title: Two pointers and sliding windows
groups.summary: Move ordered boundaries while preserving a relationship that makes discarded work unnecessary.
recognition_signals: The input is sorted, or the answer is a contiguous region whose validity changes predictably at its boundaries.
A brute-force solution repeatedly rescans pairs or overlapping ranges that differ by only one item.
common_wrong_approaches: Moving a boundary without stating the invariant can skip valid pairs or retain an invalid window.
Applying a shrinking window when negative values destroy monotonicity produces plausible but incorrect results.

problems.title: Closest Approved Spend
problems.statement: Meal prices are sorted in ascending order. Choose two different meals with the greatest combined price that does not exceed a budget. Return their indices, breaking equal sums by smaller left index and then smaller right index, or null when no pair fits.
constraints: Prices are nonnegative safe integers in sorted order
edge_cases: several pairs have the same sum

problems.title: Three-Depot Balance
problems.statement: Regional depots report signed inventory adjustments. Return every unique sorted triple of adjustment values whose sum is zero. Order triples lexicographically and do not return duplicate value combinations.

expected_complexity.space: O(n) excluding output for a sorted copy

problems.title: Shortest Throughput Burst
problems.statement: A service records positive request counts for consecutive minutes. Return the minimum number of consecutive minutes whose total is at least a required throughput, or zero if no such period exists.
constraints: Every request count is a positive safe integer
required is a positive safe integer

problems.title: Longest Reliable Run
problems.statement: A binary monitoring stream uses 1 for success and 0 for failure. Return the longest contiguous run that could be made entirely successful by reclassifying at most k failures.
edge_cases: k exceeds the number of failures

problems.title: Shared Audit Identifiers
problems.statement: Two audit systems export sorted integer identifiers, possibly with duplicates. Return the distinct identifiers present in both exports in ascending order without using a hash set.

problems.title: Maximum Retaining Span
problems.statement: Vertical flood barriers have unit-spaced positions and nonnegative heights. Choose two barriers that retain the greatest rectangular water area, defined as distance times the shorter height, and return that area.
constraints: The result fits in a safe integer

groups.title: Stacks and monotonic structures
groups.summary: Retain unresolved candidates in an order that lets one new value settle earlier decisions.
recognition_signals: The answer for an earlier item becomes known when a later larger, smaller, or conflicting item arrives.
The prompt asks for nearest boundaries, nested structure, or a window extreme without rescanning every window.
common_wrong_approaches: Scanning forward independently from every index repeats the same comparisons and becomes quadratic.
Storing values without their indices loses the distance or boundary information required for the result.

problems.title: Next Higher Sensor Reading
problems.statement: For each sensor reading, return the first strictly higher reading to its right, or -1 when no later reading is higher.

problems.title: Days Until a Higher Forecast
problems.statement: Given daily forecast temperatures, return how many days each day must wait for a strictly warmer forecast. Return zero for days with no warmer future value.

problems.title: Largest Uniform Rack Section
problems.statement: Adjacent warehouse columns have unit width and integer heights. Return the largest rectangular rack area that can fit under consecutive columns.
constraints: The result fits in a safe integer

problems.title: Minimize the Shipment Code
problems.statement: A shipment code is a decimal digit string. Remove exactly k digits while preserving the remaining order so the resulting numeric value is as small as possible. Remove leading zeros and return "0" for an empty result.

problems.title: Peak Load in Every Window
problems.statement: Given service-load readings and a positive window size, return the maximum reading in every contiguous window of that size.
constraints: 1 <= windowSize <= loads.length when loads is nonempty

problems.title: Drone Corridor Collisions
problems.statement: Drones occupy a corridor in listed left-to-right order. A positive size moves right and a negative size moves left. Opposing drones collide; the smaller absolute size is destroyed and equal sizes destroy both. Return surviving drones in order.
constraints: Drone sizes are nonzero safe integers
All drones move at equal speed

groups.title: Linked-list pointer manipulation
groups.summary: Change or compare links while preserving the part of the structure that still must be traversed.
recognition_signals: The input exposes nodes and next references rather than random-access indices or contiguous storage.
The contract requires constant auxiliary space, node reuse, or identity comparisons between shared nodes.
common_wrong_approaches: Overwriting next before saving the remaining chain disconnects nodes that still need to be processed.
Comparing node values instead of node identity gives false intersections when different nodes share a value.

problems.title: Reverse the Escalation Chain
problems.statement: An incident escalation chain is a singly linked list. Reverse its links in place and return the new head without allocating replacement nodes.

problems.title: Shared Escalation Point
problems.statement: Two acyclic escalation chains may eventually share the same node objects and suffix. Return their first shared node by identity, or null when they never intersect, using constant auxiliary space.
constraints: Combined distinct node count is at most 100000
edge_cases: equal values but no shared nodes

problems.title: Remove the Expiring Handoff
problems.statement: Remove the kth node from the end of an acyclic handoff chain and return the head. k is valid, supplied nodes must be reused, and the chain should be traversed once.

problems.title: Alternate the Support Queue
problems.statement: Reorder a support-ticket chain from L0→L1→…→Ln into L0→Ln→L1→Ln-1→… in place. Reuse nodes and return the original head.

problems.title: Symmetric Approval Chain
problems.statement: Determine whether values in an acyclic approval chain read the same forward and backward. Use constant auxiliary space and restore the chain to its original links before returning.

problems.title: Clone the Cross-Referenced Queue
problems.statement: Each queue node has next and optional related references. Return a deep clone in which every cloned reference points only to cloned nodes and the original structure remains unchanged.
constraints: related is null or points to a node in the same chain

expected_complexity.space: O(n), or O(1) auxiliary with interleaving

groups.title: Binary search and monotonic answer spaces
groups.summary: Discard half of an ordered search space by preserving the side that can still contain the answer.
recognition_signals: The data or candidate answers have an order, and a predicate changes from false to true at a boundary.
The requested scale makes a linear scan too expensive while indexed access or feasibility testing is available.
common_wrong_approaches: Using an inconsistent inclusive or half-open interval causes skipped candidates or nonterminating loops.
Returning immediately on equality is wrong when the contract asks for a first, last, minimum, or maximum boundary.

problems.title: Locate a Rotated Deployment Version
problems.primary_concept: binary search in a rotated array
problems.statement: A strictly increasing deployment-version array was rotated at an unknown pivot. Return the index of a target version or -1 when absent.

problems.title: Activation Timestamp Range
problems.statement: Given sorted activation timestamps, return the first and last indices equal to a target timestamp, or [-1, -1] if it does not occur.

problems.title: Minimum Dispatch Capacity
problems.statement: Packages must ship in their listed order over at most d days. A day carries a contiguous prefix of remaining packages up to a fixed capacity. Return the minimum capacity that completes all shipments on time.
edge_cases: capacity lower bound is the maximum weight

problems.title: Space the Access Points
problems.primary_concept: binary search on maximum feasible distance
problems.statement: Install k wireless access points at distinct candidate coordinates. Return the largest possible minimum distance between any two installed points.
constraints: Coordinates are distinct safe integers and may be unsorted

expected_complexity.time: O(n log n + n log R)

problems.title: Search the Sharded Metric Matrix
problems.statement: Each matrix row is sorted, and the first value of a row is greater than the final value of the previous row. Return whether a target metric appears without flattening the matrix.

problems.title: Median Across Two Telemetry Streams
problems.statement: Two telemetry arrays are individually sorted. Return the median of all values without fully merging them, in logarithmic time with respect to the shorter array.
constraints: At least one array is nonempty
edge_cases: all values in one array precede the other

groups.title: Recursion and backtracking
groups.summary: Explore a decision tree while restoring mutable choice state before trying the next branch.
recognition_signals: The prompt asks for all valid constructions, combinations, permutations, or placements under constraints.
A partial choice can be extended recursively and rejected early when it can no longer lead to a solution.
common_wrong_approaches: Forgetting to undo a choice leaks state between sibling branches and silently removes or corrupts results.
Copying large state at every branch can turn an already exponential search into avoidable extra overhead.

problems.title: Choose the On-Call Team
problems.statement: Given distinct engineer IDs and team size k, return every size-k team while preserving input order within each team. Order teams by the depth-first choice order induced by the input.

problems.title: Feature Rollout Orders
problems.statement: Given distinct feature flags, return every possible rollout order. Each output must use every flag exactly once.
edge_cases: empty input has one empty order

problems.title: Support Keypad Messages
problems.statement: Digits 2 through 9 map to their standard telephone keypad letters. Return every possible letter message represented by an input digit string, or an empty array for an empty input.
edge_cases: digits seven and nine have four letters

problems.title: Trace a Command Through the Grid
problems.statement: Determine whether a command string can be traced through orthogonally adjacent grid cells. A cell may be used at most once in one trace, and matching is case-sensitive.
constraints: Do not leave the grid mutated

problems.title: Place Noninterfering Replicas
problems.statement: Place n service replicas on an n-by-n grid so no two share a row, column, or diagonal. Return the number of distinct placements.
constraints: Each row contains exactly one replica
Reflections and rotations count as distinct placements

problems.title: Restore Network Address Segments
problems.statement: Insert three separators into a decimal digit string to form four address segments. Each segment must be 0 through 255 and may not contain a leading zero unless it is exactly "0". Return all valid addresses.
constraints: Output addresses must preserve digit order
edge_cases: too few or too many digits

groups.title: Tree traversal and structural recursion
groups.summary: Combine answers from child subtrees or process nodes by depth while respecting tree invariants.
recognition_signals: The input is hierarchical and each node naturally owns independent left and right subproblems.
The requested property depends on ancestor bounds, root-to-node paths, subtree summaries, or level order.
common_wrong_approaches: Checking only a node against its immediate children misses violations inherited from more distant ancestors.
Recomputing subtree height or contents at every node turns a linear traversal into quadratic work on skewed trees.

problems.title: Validate the Routing Index Tree
problems.statement: Determine whether a binary routing tree is a valid strict binary-search tree: every value in a left subtree is smaller and every value in a right subtree is larger than its ancestor. Duplicate values are invalid.
edge_cases: deep descendant violates an ancestor bound

problems.title: Closest Shared Manager
problems.statement: Given a binary organization tree and two existing employee nodes, return their lowest shared manager. A node may be its own ancestor, and matching uses node identity.
constraints: Both target nodes exist in the tree
The tree is not necessarily a search tree and height is at most 1000
edge_cases: one target is ancestor of the other

problems.title: Count Target-Cost Reporting Paths
problems.statement: Each hierarchy node has a signed cost. Count downward ancestor-to-descendant paths whose values sum to target. A path may start and end at any nodes but must follow parent-to-child links.
constraints: Costs and target are safe integers
The answer fits in a safe integer and tree height is at most 1000

expected_complexity.space: O(h) average map entries, O(n) worst case

problems.title: Rightmost Service by Tier
problems.statement: Return the rightmost service value at every depth of a binary hierarchy, from the root level downward.
constraints: Preserve the tree; tree height is at most 1000

expected_complexity.space: O(w), where w is maximum width

problems.title: Longest Handoff Route
problems.statement: Return the maximum number of edges on any path between two nodes in a binary handoff hierarchy. The path does not need to pass through the root.

problems.title: Rebuild the Deployment Hierarchy
problems.statement: Reconstruct and return a binary deployment tree from its preorder and inorder value sequences. All values are distinct and the sequences describe one valid tree.
constraints: Preorder and inorder have equal length
All values are distinct safe integers and tree height is at most 1000
edge_cases: root split at an inorder boundary

groups.title: Heaps and streaming selection
groups.summary: Retain the next most relevant candidate without fully ordering all available data.
recognition_signals: The prompt repeatedly needs the smallest, largest, earliest, or kth item while data changes over time.
Only a bounded subset of candidates matters, or several already ordered streams must be merged incrementally.
common_wrong_approaches: Sorting the complete collection after every update repeats work that a heap maintains incrementally.
Using the wrong heap direction retains the items that should be discarded and breaks bounded top-k logic.

problems.title: Running Median Latency
problems.statement: Latency measurements arrive one at a time. Return the median after every insertion; for an even number of measurements, use the average of the two middle values.
constraints: Returned averages are exact halves when necessary

problems.title: Merge Regional Telemetry Streams
problems.statement: Several regions provide sorted telemetry arrays. Merge them into one sorted array while keeping at most one pending candidate from each region in a priority queue.

problems.title: Assign Jobs to Available Workers
problems.statement: Workers have integer weights and process one job at a time. Jobs arrive at integer times equal to their indices and have durations. Assign each job to the available worker with smallest weight then index, or wait for the earliest worker to finish. Return assigned worker indices.
constraints: Weights and durations are positive safe integers

problems.title: Nearest Service Depots
problems.statement: Given depot coordinates and k, return the k depots closest to the origin. Compare squared distance, then x, then y; return the selected depots in that order.
constraints: Coordinates and squared distances are safe integers

expected_complexity.time: O(n log k + k log k)

problems.title: Online Kth-Highest Throughput
problems.statement: Given k and a stream of throughput readings, return the kth-highest reading after each insertion once at least k readings have arrived; return null for earlier prefixes.

problems.title: Separate Repeated Job Categories
problems.statement: Reorder job category strings so no equal categories are adjacent. Return the lexicographically smallest valid arrangement among choices available at each greedy step, or null if no arrangement exists.

groups.title: Graph search and connectivity
groups.summary: Model relationships explicitly, then choose traversal order and state according to the requested path or component property.
recognition_signals: Entities have arbitrary many-to-many relationships, dependencies, routes, or grid neighbors rather than a hierarchy.
The prompt asks about reachability, ordering, connected groups, shortest paths, or merging transitively related records.
common_wrong_approaches: Marking visited at the wrong time can enqueue a node repeatedly or block a cheaper weighted route discovered later.
Using depth-first discovery depth as a shortest-path distance is invalid when traversal order does not preserve distance.

problems.title: Deployment Dependency Order
problems.statement: Services are numbered 0 through n - 1. Each dependency [service, prerequisite] requires the prerequisite first. Return the lexicographically smallest valid deployment order, or an empty array when a cycle makes deployment impossible.

expected_complexity.time: O((V + E) log V) for lexical ordering

problems.title: Cheapest Route with Transfer Limit
problems.statement: Directed routes have nonnegative prices. Return the cheapest price from source to destination using at most k intermediate transfers, or -1 when no such route exists.
edge_cases: cheapest unrestricted route exceeds the limit

problems.title: Incident Propagation Time
problems.statement: A grid contains blocked cells, healthy services, and initially failed services. Each minute, failures spread orthogonally to healthy neighbors. Return minutes until no healthy service remains, or -1 if some can never fail.
constraints: Cells are blocked, healthy, or failed
Do not mutate the input grid

problems.title: Clone the Service Dependency Graph
problems.statement: Given a node in a connected undirected service graph, return a deep clone. Cloned adjacency order must match the original, cloned edges must reference only clones, and the original graph must remain unchanged.
constraints: The graph may contain cycles and self-edges
edge_cases: duplicate node values require identity mapping

problems.title: Merge Customer Identity Records
problems.statement: Each customer record contains a display name followed by one or more email addresses. Records sharing any email belong to the same customer. Merge transitively connected records, sorting emails and ordering results by smallest original record index.
constraints: All records in one component use the same display name

problems.title: Lowest-Risk Grid Route
problems.statement: Each grid cell has a nonnegative entry risk. Starting at the top-left, move orthogonally to the bottom-right and return the minimum total risk of entered cells, including both endpoints.
constraints: The result fits in a safe integer
edge_cases: cheapest route is not shortest by edges

groups.title: Dynamic programming and greedy decisions
groups.summary: Identify reusable subproblem state, or prove that one locally safe choice leaves an optimal remainder.
recognition_signals: A brute-force decision tree revisits the same suffix, amount, position, or previous-choice state many times.
The answer is an optimum or count built from smaller prefixes, unless an exchange argument supports a greedy choice.
common_wrong_approaches: Memoizing incomplete state combines subproblems that have different future options and returns incorrect optima.
Choosing the locally largest or smallest option without an exchange proof often fails on carefully spaced counterexamples.

problems.title: Minimum Tokens for an Exact Refund
problems.statement: Given positive token denominations and a refund amount, return the fewest tokens needed to total the amount exactly, or -1 when it is impossible. Each denomination may be used repeatedly.

problems.title: Decode the Compact Badge Message
problems.statement: Digits encode letters with 1 through 26 mapping to A through Z. Return the number of ways to decode a nonempty digit string; zero cannot be decoded alone.
constraints: The result fits in a safe integer

problems.title: Longest Improving Performance Trend
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of performance scores. Selected scores need not be contiguous, and equal scores do not increase the sequence.

problems.title: Segment the Service Alias
problems.statement: Determine whether a service alias can be segmented into one or more dictionary tokens. Tokens may be reused, matching is case-sensitive, and the complete alias must be consumed.
constraints: Total dictionary characters are at most 100000

expected_complexity.time: O(nL) with bounded maximum token length L

edge_cases: prefix choices that lead to dead ends

problems.title: Schedule the Most Maintenance Jobs
problems.statement: Maintenance jobs use half-open intervals [start, end). Select the maximum number of non-overlapping jobs one technician can complete. Return selected original indices in execution order, breaking equal end times by smaller original index.
constraints: Times are safe integers with start <= end

problems.title: Minimum Cost Through Checkpoints
problems.statement: Each checkpoint has an entry cost. Starting before checkpoint 0, you may move one or two checkpoints at a time and pay the cost of each checkpoint landed on. Return the minimum cost to move beyond the final checkpoint.
constraints: The result fits in a safe integer
edge_cases: locally cheaper step leads to larger total
